title: Effect of humic acid application on crop yield
research_question: Does exogenous humic acid (humic substances) application increase crop yield compared to untreated controls?

population.description: Field and greenhouse crops treated with humic acid or humic substances

intervention.description: Exogenous application of humic acid, humic substances, or humate products (soil or foliar)

comparator.description: No humic acid application (untreated control or equivalent fertilizer without humic acid)
comparator.definition: Same crop grown without humic acid/humate addition

primary.description: Crop yield (grain yield, fruit yield, tuber yield, biomass yield)
primary.direction_of_interest: positive (humic acid expected to increase yield)

intervention: Humic acid / humic substances application (soil or foliar)
primary_outcomes: Crop yield (grain yield, fruit yield, tuber yield, biomass per unit area)
important_moderators: Humic acid source (leonardite, compost extract, vermicompost, commercial product)
Application method (soil drench, foliar spray, seed treatment, fertigation)
Crop type (cereal, vegetable, legume, fruit, root/tuber)
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Extract yield for BOTH humic acid treatment AND untreated control
2. Control = no humic acid; Treatment = with humic acid/humate
3. If multiple rates tested, extract EACH rate vs the same control separately
5. Record humic acid source, application method, and rate
6. Focus on CROP YIELD as primary outcome, not plant height/root length/chlorophyll
tc_confusion_warnings: Control is the NO humic acid treatment (may still receive mineral fertilizer)
Treatment is WITH humic acid (may also receive mineral fertilizer)
Some papers test humic acid + NPK combinations - extract HA+NPK vs NPK (isolate HA effect)
Fulvic acid is sometimes reported separately from humic acid - include both
Do NOT confuse with compost or organic amendment trials where humic acid is not the isolated variable
Watch for humic acid concentration units (mg/L for foliar vs kg/ha for soil)

search.seed_papers_description: Ma, Cheng & Zhang 2024 (Agronomy MDPI, meta-analysis of humic acid fertilizer effects on crop yield and NUE, 93 articles, 383 yield observations)

inclusion_criteria: Primary experiment comparing humic acid/humate treatment vs untreated control
Reports yield or biomass data (numeric means)
Humic acid is the isolated experimental variable (not confounded with other amendments)
Includes both treatment and control groups
exclusion_criteria: Humic acid not isolated as experimental variable
No yield or biomass data reported
Only reports plant height, root length, or physiological traits without yield

published_pooled_effect.notes: +12% yield increase from humic acid fertilizer. Also: +27% NUE, +17% N uptake. Cash crops and upland cereals better than paddy rice. Optimal at 100-200 kg N/ha. MDPI fully open access.

notes: Selected as V2 pilot topic: fully OA, clean estimand, never tested, moderate corpus size
